clue.text: One's ration by the bar is taken to avoid a threat

definitions.note: describes an action, a step taken in defence

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: a bar in a pub or shop is a counter
a ration, one's allowance, is a measure

explanation.surface: Someone takes their drink allowance at the bar to steer clear of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermeasure is a step adopted to neutralise a danger, i.e. something done to ward off a threat.

clue.text: Written authority to meet family in school

parts.note: a charter is a written grant of rights or authority
a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A document of authority is presented to a family at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARTERHOUSE is a well-known English private (public) school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is the name of a famous English boarding school, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Relation sometimes of use to the penniless

definitions.text: sometimes of use to the penniless
definitions.meaning: old slang for a pawnbroker, to whom the hard-up pledge goods for cash

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a parent's brother, and in old slang a pawnbroker, who lends money to the broke.

clue.text: Argos tent redesigned: each one has four sides

indicators.note: something redesigned is laid out anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tent from the Argos catalogue has been redesigned with a four-sided layout.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is a British catalogue store. 'redesigned' rearranges ARGOSTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetragons are four-sided plane figures, quadrilaterals, so each such shape has four edges.

clue.text: Muttering on stage about edible stalks, repeatedly

definitions.meaning: the word actors say over and over to simulate background crowd chatter
a garden plant whose pink stems are cooked as fruit

explanation.surface: Actors murmur about vegetables over and over on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'repeatedly' tie the senses together: stage extras repeat this word to sound like a murmuring crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a plant grown for its tart stems, and also the nonsense word crowds of actors mumble.

clue.text: Beethoven's moth?

definitions.meaning: Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto carries this regal nickname
a large silk moth, Saturnia pavonia, has this imperial name

explanation.definitionFit: It is the nickname of Beethoven's fifth piano concerto and the name of a large British moth species.

clue.text: Guitar sound gives the street spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Music from a guitar makes the street feel lively.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to brush the strings of a guitar, and the noise produced is a strumming sound.

clue.text: Such a to-do makes a girl more troubled

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fuss is making a young woman even more upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a tiresome, long-winded procedure, a fuss or palaver.

clue.text: Sandy is, perhaps, seen at this racecourse

definitions.text: Sandy is, perhaps, seen at this racecourse

parts.words: Sandy is, perhaps, seen at this racecourse
parts.note: Sandy is a stereotypically Scottish name, so Sandy might be described as one native of Scotland; that description, written as one word, names the venue

explanation.surface: Somebody named Sandy turns up at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy (short for Alexander) is a typically Scottish name; ASCOT is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a well-known horse-racing venue in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Decision by third person (ie a grump) is incorrect

indicators.note: letters that are incorrect are out of place, so they are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A grumpy person makes a wrong judgement as the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpirage is the arbitration of an umpire, a neutral third party who decides between two sides.

clue.text: At no time must they be chopped off smaller still

parts.note: never means at no time

indicators.note: the word they loses its last letter, the tail being chopped away

parts.note: less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: They must never be cut down any smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as a conjunction meaning all the same or however, is a synonym.

clue.text: Subjects requiring one to be on the carpet

indicators.note: in an across clue, being on something means coming after it

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet
a means one

explanation.surface: A subject who needs disciplining is to be summoned before the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the carpet' is an idiom for being called in for a reprimand, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Themata is the plural of thema, a learned word for a theme or topic, so subjects.

clue.text: A politician in a frenzy may be seen to run riot

indicators.note: the first pieces sit in the middle of the second

parts.note: a rage is a frenzy
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A furious politician is seen running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush around violently, to run riot; both phrases are verbs.

clue.text: Priest almost always found to be right in book

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman is nearly always right according to the book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, as opposed to the verso.

clue.text: A late crop scattered by Egyptian ruler

indicators.note: scattered means strewn around, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A late harvest is spread about by a Pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was a queen of ancient Egypt, the last active Ptolemaic ruler.

clue.text: Song composed by girl getting undressed outside

indicators.note: the word for undressed goes outside the girl's name

parts.note: bare means undressed
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A song is written by a woman who is stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a song of Venetian gondoliers, or music imitating one.

clue.text: Name of US car belonging to King George and A.P. Herbert

parts.note: auto is American for a car
GR is Georgius Rex, King George
the writer A. P. Herbert's initials are APH

explanation.surface: The signature on an American car belonging to the King and a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: A. P. Herbert was an English humorist and MP; his three initials form the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's signature, their name written in their own hand.

clue.text: "Wild Rose" contains poetry for managers

indicators.note: the scrambled flower holds the poetry word inside
wild means unruly, so these letters run out of order

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A song called Wild Rose has poetic lyrics for its bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild Rose' reads as a song title, but 'Wild' is the anagram signal, giving OERS, and 'contains' is a container signal, not a description of lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseers are supervisors, people who direct workers, i.e. managers.

clue.text: Each unfinished nap's most comfortable

indicators.note: unfinished means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: Each nap left uncompleted is the most relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest means most at ease or least demanding, hence most comfortable.

clue.text: Do I fast after cooking this Greek dish?

indicators.note: cooking means mixing up, so after this treatment the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether to fast once this Greek dish is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifado is a Greek stew of beef or rabbit with onions, a traditional Greek meal.

clue.text: What is pinching the foot?

parts.note: the is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is squeezing their foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like tight shoes; in slang to pinch is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinching is slang for stealing, and the act of stealing is a crime of that name.

clue.text: Son's nursing a broken hip but anyone could get water with these

definitions.text: anyone could get water with these

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: son's read as son is gives SONS

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son looks after a fractured hip, while anyone could fetch water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' gives IPH; the surface's injured hip and 'nursing' as care mislead, since 'nursing' is just a container signal and the definition is the long tail of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Siphons are tubes that draw liquid up and over, so they are devices for drawing water.

clue.text: Decoration only half seen, being bulky

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is an honour

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: A medal is only partly visible because the wearer is so large.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, so heavily built or bulky.

clue.text: One who won't thank you for this stylish jar

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish
to grate is to jar or irritate

explanation.surface: Someone will not be grateful for this fashionable pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, someone who shows no thanks.

clue.text: Perfume's what makes a wooer finally love mother

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A suitor wears scent to win his beloved's mother over.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a fragrance or perfume.

clue.text: Last of all, the rest may help you

definitions.text: Last of all, the rest may help you

parts.words: Last of all, the rest may help you
parts.note: a Latin tag written at the very end of a list stands for all the remaining items, sparing the writer

explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera means and the rest, placed at the end of a list to save naming everything.

clue.text: Without the doctor, Leonard could be in such a state

indicators.note: could be means the letters remaining might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Leonard, left without his physician, might feel isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes DR from LEONARD, leaving LEONA, which 'could be' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone means on one's own, solitary, the state of someone with no companion.

clue.text: Be a likely winner, choosing left or right?

definitions.text: Be a likely winner, choosing left or right?

parts.words: Be a likely winner, choosing left or right?
parts.note: someone who backs both options of a choice cannot lose whichever turns out correct

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to gain from two opposing positions at once, so you win whichever way things go.
